rationale: Original Spanish paper describes dose-dependent CNS suppression after injection of fresh allspice leaf extracts. Its oral fraction experiment measures vital signs and weight. It did not assess mood or culinary ground berries.

Five men developed neuropathy during use of Tartarian buckwheat products for diabetes. The authors describe dyskinesia without operational detail in the available abstract. The species and unspecified product differ from toasted common groats.
Uses boiled buckwheat porridge to stimulate gallbladder contraction before ultrasound. Dyskinesia refers to the biliary tract and gallbladder.

Nigella oil mouth rinse was compared with magic mouthwash in AML chemotherapy. Day 28 normal diet was reported for 26/27 versus 20/25 (p=.159), after favorable earlier results. Ground nigella and neurogenic dysphagia were not tested.
Curcumin plus piperine versus placebo gave no clear between-group Epworth sleepiness result (p=.83) in women with premenstrual symptoms and dysmenorrhea.
Example 15 uses oregano extract in an effervescent lozenge. Salivation is part of the described generic dosage-form action and is not a clinical drooling estimate for fresh oregano.
Multi-ingredient medicine includes doukou and claims relief of malignant obstruction and difficulty swallowing. Original claims and examples supply no isolated ground green cardamom comparison.
Uncontrolled Alzheimer's cohort reports lower apathy ratings after sublingual cannabis extract with unspecified olive-oil carrier. No oil-only arm. The same cohort was described in the 2022 preprint.
Earlier version of the same 30-patient uncontrolled cannabis study. Apathy change cannot isolate olive oil, and the oil processing is unspecified.
